newsitem.title: USA: Florida sees no immediate effect from S&P upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Florida sees no immediate effect from S&P upgrade.

text.p: Florida's bond chief said he was "very pleased" with Standard & Poor's upgrade of the state's general obligation bond rating, but did not expect to see an immediate impact.
"It's great. It's wonderful news," said Ben Watkins, director of the Florida Division of Bond Finance. "We're very pleased with it but I don't expect to see an immediate impact."
S&P raised Florida's GO bond rating to AA-plus from AA on Thursday, a move that affects $8.2 billion of bond debt.
The state has no GO bond sales pending but expects to issue $200 million of Board of Education Public Education Capital Outlay GOs in late summer or early fall.

Florida also has authorization to issue $350 million of Department of Transportation Right of Way Aquisition GO bonds and expects to issue some of that this summer, though it may be split into two issues.

Even when those deals come to market, it would be hard to pinpoint the effect of the upgrade, Watkins said. The S&P upgrade gives Florida a split rating, with Moody's Investors Service and Fitch Investors Service keeping their ratings at AA.
Florida GO bonds typically price at AAA levels anyway, especially at the short end up to 10 years, Watkins said.

"Rating is just one of many factors that goes into pricing. You've got to consider market conditions, the structure of the bid," Watkins said. "To come up with a number, what level of savings, I don't think you can quantify it with any degree of accuracy."
Traders also said they had seen no effect on Florida bonds in the secondary market after the upgrade, with no major blocks of Florida GOs trading.

Florida has two revenue bond issues on the day-to-day calendar, which were not expected to be affected by the upgrade -- $300 million of Department of Environmental Protection Preservation 2000 bonds, and $36.8 million of Board of Regents University System Improvement Revenue Bonds. Both are to be sold by competitive bid with 20 hours notice.
